paragraphs: Teacher Kim's class made a magazine for the school. On Thursday, Lily wrote the contents page in the library. A contents page shows what is in the magazine and on which page. Mia and Leo sat next to Lily and gave her ideas. "Is the list ready?" asked Leo. "Almost," said Lily. "I only need the page numbers and the titles."

Here is the first half of the list. "Page two: A Letter from Teacher Kim." "Page three: Our Local Market, an article by Mia." "Page five: Geography Corner. Where is Thailand on the map?" "Page six: Never Walk Alone. Five Ways to Stay Safe." "Page seven: Leo's Cartoon. A boy and his bad day." Mia read the list and smiled. "My article is on page three," she said.

Here is the second half of the list. "Page eight: Join the Club! Fill in the form." "Page nine: A Good Excuse. A Funny Story by May." "Page ten: Afterwards. Games for After School." "Page eleven: Photos of the Month." Lily checked each page number two times. Leo thought that his cartoon was on page nine. "Leo, your cartoon is on page seven, not page nine," she said. "Page nine is the story by May."

Leo looked at the list and asked about the photos. "Do the photos have captions?" he asked. "Yes, they do," said Mia. "Under the market photo on page three, there is a short caption." The caption says "The market at seven o'clock." "On page eleven, each photo has a short caption, too," said Lily. "The form on page eight has a note, too." The note says "Write your name here." "A contents page and a caption are small, but they help everybody," said Lily.

Afterwards, Lily gave the page to Teacher Kim. Teacher Kim read the titles and the page numbers carefully. "This is clear and easy to read," she said. "The titles are short, and the page numbers are in order." "Which page do you want to read first, Mia?" "Page seven," said Mia, "because I love Leo's cartoons." Leo laughed and said, "I will draw a cartoon of you, Mia!"
